A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified a mechanism for regulating the expression of the virulence genes that are required for Agrobacterium to cause tumors on plants.

the expression of virulence genes is a highly regulated process that is integrated into the physiology of the cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regulation of bacterial virulence is integrated with the regulation of the cellular defense activities that protect against toxic compounds, including those produced by the plant.
the expression of virulence genes in a plant pathogen is not a wasteful activity, even when the pathogen is in an environment in which it would not be expected to encounter a host plant.
